title.zh: 卷一百二十 列傳第八 諸王五
title.raw: 卷一百二十 列傳第八 諸王五 Volume 120 Biographies 8: Princes 5

sentences.zh: 諸王五○世宗諸子

translations.literal: Princes 5 ○ Sons of the Shizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Princes 5: Sons of the Jiajing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 哀沖太子載基莊敬太子載景王載圳潁王載戚王載沴薊王載㙺均王載𰉬○穆宗諸子

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ai Chong Zai Ji; Crown Prince Zhuang Jing Zai He; Prince Jing Zai Zhen; Prince Ying Zai Yan; Prince Qi Zai Lin; Prince Ji Zai Zhu; Prince Jun Zai Su ○ Sons of the Muzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ai Chong (Zai Ji); Crown Prince Zhuang Jing (Zai He); Prince Jing (Zai Zhen); Prince Ying (Zai Yan); Prince Qi (Zai Lin); Prince Ji (Zai Zhu); Prince Jun (Zai Su) — sons of the Longqing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 憲懷太子翊釴靖王翊鈴潞王翊镠○神宗諸子

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xian Huai Yi Xi; Prince Jing Yi Ling; Prince Lu Yi Liu ○ Sons of the Shenzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xian Huai (Yi Xi); Prince Jing (Yi Ling); Prince Lu (Yi Liu) — sons of the Wanli Emperor.

sentences.zh: 邠王常漵福王常洵沅王常治瑞王常浩惠王常潤桂王常瀛○光宗諸子

translations.literal: Prince Bin Chang Xu; Prince Fu Chang Xun; Prince Yuan Chang Zhi; Prince Rui Chang Hao; Prince Hui Chang Run; Prince Gui Chang Ying ○ Sons of the Guangzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bin (Chang Xu); Prince Fu (Chang Xun); Prince Yuan (Chang Zhi); Prince Rui (Chang Hao); Prince Hui (Chang Run); Prince Gui (Chang Ying) — sons of the Taichang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 簡王由學齊王由楫懷王田模湘王由栩惠王由橏○熹宗諸子

translations.literal: Prince Jian You Xue; Prince Qi You Ji; Prince Huai You Mo; Prince Xiang You Xu; Prince Hui You Rong ○ Sons of the Xizong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian (You Xue); Prince Qi (You Ji); Prince Huai (You Mo); Prince Xiang (You Xu); Prince Hui (You Rong) — sons of the Tianqi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 懷沖太子慈然悼懷太子慈焴獻懷太子慈炅○莊烈帝諸子

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huai Chong Ci Ran; Crown Prince Dao Huai Ci Yu; Crown Prince Xian Huai Ci Jiong ○ Sons of the Zhuanglie Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huai Chong (Ci Ran); Crown Prince Dao Huai (Ci Yu); Crown Prince Xian Huai (Ci Jiong) — sons of the Chongzhen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 太子慈烺懷王慈烜定王慈炯永王慈照悼靈王慈煥悼懷王

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ci Lang; Prince Huai Ci Xuan; Prince Ding Ci Jiong; Prince Yong Ci Zhao; Prince Dao Ling Ci Huan; Prince Dao Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ci Lang; Prince Huai (Ci Xuan); Prince Ding (Ci Jiong); Prince Yong (Ci Zhao); Prince Dao Ling (Ci Huan); Prince Dao Huai.

sentences.zh: 世宗八子。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiajing Emperor had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 閻貴妃生哀沖太子載基。

translations.literal: Consort Yan the Noble Consort bore Crown Prince Ai Chong Zai Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yan bore Crown Prince Ai Chong (Zai Ji).

sentences.zh: 王貴妃生莊敬太子載。

translations.literal: Consort Wang the Noble Consort bore Crown Prince Zhuang Jing Zai He.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang bore Crown Prince Zhuang Jing (Zai He).

sentences.zh: 杜太后生穆宗。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Du bore the Muzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Du bore the Longqing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 盧靖妃生景王載圳。

translations.literal: Consort Lu Jing bore Prince Jing Zai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Lu Jing bore Prince Jing (Zai Zhen).

sentences.zh: 江肅妃生潁王載。

translations.literal: Consort Jiang Su bore Prince Ying Zai Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Jiang Su bore Prince Ying (Zai Yan).

sentences.zh: 趙懿妃生戚王載沴。

translations.literal: Consort Zhao Yi bore Prince Qi Zai Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhao Yi bore Prince Qi (Zai Lin).

sentences.zh: 陳雍妃生薊王載㙺。

translations.literal: Consort Chen Yong bore Prince Ji Zai Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Chen Yong bore Prince Ji (Zai Zhu).

sentences.zh: 趙榮妃生均王載𰉬。

translations.literal: Consort Zhao Rong bore Prince Jun Zai Su.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhao Rong bore Prince Jun (Zai Su).

sentences.zh: 哀沖太子載基，世宗第一子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ai Chong Zai Ji was the Shizong Emperor's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ai Chong (Zai Ji) was the Jiajing Emperor's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 生二月而殤。

translations.literal: He lived two months and then died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: He lived only two months before dying in infancy.

sentences.zh: 莊敬太子載，世宗第二子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhuang Jing Zai He was the Shizong Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhuang Jing (Zai He) was the Jiajing Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年，世宗將南巡，立為皇太子，甫四歲，命監國，以大學士夏言為傅。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing, when the Shizong Emperor was about to tour the south, he was invested as crown prince at the age of only four; he was ordered to oversee the realm, and Grand Secretary Xia Yan was appointed his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of the Jiajing reign, as the emperor prepared a southern tour, the four-year-old prince was invested as crown prince and charged with overseeing the realm; Grand Secretary Xia Yan was appointed his tutor.

sentences.zh: 尚書霍韜、郎中鄒守益獻《東宮聖學圖冊》，疑為謗訕，幾獲罪。

translations.literal: Minister Huo Tao and Section Director Zou Shouyi presented the Illustrated Manual of Sacred Learning for the Eastern Palace; it was suspected of being slanderous, and they nearly incurred punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Huo Tao and section director Zou Shouyi presented the Illustrated Manual of Sacred Learning for the Eastern Palace; the work was suspected of slander, and they nearly faced punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝既得方士段朝用，思習修攝術，諭禮部，具皇太子監國儀。

translations.literal: Once the emperor had obtained the Daoist adept Duan Chaoyong, he wished to study the arts of cultivation and longevity, and instructed the Ministry of Rites to draw up the protocol for the crown prince's regency.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor acquired the Daoist adept Duan Chaoyong and set his mind on learning cultivation and longevity techniques, he instructed the Ministry of Rites to prepare the protocol for a crown-prince regency.

sentences.zh: 太仆卿楊最諫，杖死，監國之議亦罷。

translations.literal: Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Yang Zui remonstrated and was beaten to death; the proposal for a regency was also abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Yang Zui remonstrated and was beaten to death, and the regency proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 贊善羅洪先、趙時春、唐順之請太子出閤，講學文華殿，皆削籍。

translations.literal: Palace Lecturers Luo Hongxian, Zhao Shichun, and Tang Shunzhi requested that the crown prince leave his quarters and study in the Wenhua Hall; all were struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Palace lecturers Luo Hongxian, Zhao Shichun, and Tang Shunzhi asked that the crown prince leave his quarters to study in Wenhua Hall; all were struck from the official registers.

sentences.zh: 太廟成，命太子攝祀。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, the crown prince was ordered to preside at the sacrifices in the emperor's stead.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Ancestral Temple was completed, the crown prince was ordered to preside at the sacrifices on the emperor's behalf.

sentences.zh: 二十八年三月行寇禮，越二日薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-eighth year he performed the capping ceremony; two days later he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-eighth year he underwent the capping ceremony, and two days later he died.

sentences.zh: 帝命與哀沖太子並建寢園，歲時祭祀，從諸陵後。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that a burial park be built jointly for him and Crown Prince Ai Chong, with seasonal sacrifices following after those at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a burial park built for him alongside Crown Prince Ai Chong, with seasonal sacrifices performed after those at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 景恭王載圳，世宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Gong Zai Zhen was the Shizong Emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Gong (Zai Zhen) was the Jiajing Emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十八年冊立太子，同日封穆宗裕王、載圳景王。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing the crown prince was formally invested; on the same day the Muzong Emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu and Zai Zhen as Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Jiajing the crown prince was formally invested, and on the same day the future Longqing Emperor was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu while Zai Zhen was enfeoffed as Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 其後太子薨，廷臣言裕王次當立。

translations.literal: Afterward the crown prince died, and court officials said the Prince of Yu, being next in line, ought to be invested.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince died, court officials argued that the Prince of Yu, as next in line, ought to be invested as heir.

sentences.zh: 帝以前太子不永，遲之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the former crown prince had not lived long, delayed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Because the previous crown prince had died young, the emperor delayed the decision.

sentences.zh: 晚信方士語，二王皆不得見。

translations.literal: In his later years he believed the words of Daoist adepts, and neither prince was allowed an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, swayed by Daoist adepts, he refused audiences to both princes.

sentences.zh: 載圳既與裕王並出邸，居處衣服無別。

translations.literal: Once Zai Zhen had left the palace together with the Prince of Yu, their dwellings and dress were indistinguishable.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zai Zhen left the palace together with the Prince of Yu, their residences and attire were made indistinguishable.

sentences.zh: 載圳年少，左右懷窺覬，語漸聞，中外頗有異論。

translations.literal: Zai Zhen was young, and those around him harbored designs on the succession; word gradually spread, and there was considerable dissent inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Zhen was still young, and those around him nursed ambitions for the succession; rumors spread, and dissent arose both inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 四十年之國德安。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he went to his fief at De'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he went to take up his fief at De'an.

sentences.zh: 居四年薨。

translations.literal: After four years in residence he died.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died.

sentences.zh: 帝謂大學士徐階曰：「此子素謀奪嫡，今死矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Grand Secretary Xu Jie: "This son has long plotted to seize the succession; now he is dead."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Grand Secretary Xu Jie, "This son has long plotted to seize the succession. Now he is dead."

sentences.zh: 初，載圳之藩，多請莊田。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zai Zhen went to his fief, he repeatedly requested estate lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai Zhen first went to his fief, he repeatedly requested estate lands.

sentences.zh: 部議給之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and granted them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved the grants.

sentences.zh: 荊州沙市不在請中。

translations.literal: Shashi in Jingzhou was not among the lands requested.
translations.idiomatic: Shashi in Jingzhou was not among the lands he had requested.

sentences.zh: 中使責市租，知府徐學謨執不與，又取薪稅於漢陽之劉家塥，推官吳宗周持之，皆獲譴。

translations.literal: A palace envoy demanded market rents; Prefect Xu Xuemo firmly refused to hand them over; they also collected firewood taxes at Liujiahe in Hanyang, and Assistant Magistrate Wu Zongzhou resisted — all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: A palace envoy demanded market rents, but Prefect Xu Xuemo refused to comply; when the prince's agents also levied firewood taxes at Liujiahe in Hanyang and Assistant Magistrate Wu Zongzhou resisted, all were punished.

sentences.zh: 其他土田湖陂侵入者數萬頃。

translations.literal: Other fields, ponds, and embankments seized amounted to tens of thousands of qing.
translations.idiomatic: Other seized fields, ponds, and embankments amounted to tens of thousands of qing.

sentences.zh: 王無子，歸葬西山，妃妾皆還居京邸，封除。

translations.literal: The prince had no sons; he was buried at Xishan, his consorts and concubines all returned to reside at the capital residence, and the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The prince left no sons; he was buried at Xishan, his consorts and concubines returned to the capital residence, and the princely line was abolished.

sentences.zh: 潁殤王載，世宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Ying Shang Zai Yan was the Shizong Emperor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying Shang (Zai Yan) was the Jiajing Emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 生未逾月殤。

translations.literal: He lived less than a month and died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: He lived less than a month before dying in infancy.

sentences.zh: 戚懷王載沴，世宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Huai Zai Lin was the Shizong Emperor's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Huai (Zai Lin) was the Jiajing Emperor's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 薊哀王載㙺，世宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Ji Ai Zai Zhu was the Shizong Emperor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ji Ai (Zai Zhu) was the Jiajing Emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 均思王載𰉬，世宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince Jun Si Zai Su was the Shizong Emperor's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun Si (Zai Su) was the Jiajing Emperor's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 三王俱未逾歲殤，追加封謚。

translations.literal: All three princes died in infancy before reaching one year of age, and posthumous titles and enfeoffments were added.
translations.idiomatic: All three died in infancy before their first year, and posthumous titles and enfeoffments were conferred.

sentences.zh: 穆宗四子。

translations.literal: The Muzong Emperor had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Longqing Emperor had four sons.

sentences.zh: 李皇后生憲懷太子翊釴，孝定太后生神宗、潞王翊镠，其靖王翊鈴，母氏無考。

translations.literal: Empress Li bore Crown Prince Xian Huai Yi Xi; Empress Dowager Xiaoding bore the Shenzong Emperor and Prince Lu Yi Liu; as for Prince Jing Yi Ling, his mother is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li bore Crown Prince Xian Huai (Yi Xi); Empress Dowager Xiaoding bore the Wanli Emperor and Prince Lu (Yi Liu); Prince Jing (Yi Ling)'s mother is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 憲懷太子翊釴，穆宗長子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xian Huai Yi Xi was the Muzong Emperor's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xian Huai (Yi Xi) was the Longqing Emperor's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 生五歲殤，贈裕世子。

translations.literal: He lived five years and died in infancy; he was posthumously granted the title of Heir of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy at the age of five and was posthumously granted the title Heir of Yu.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年追謚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing a posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous title was conferred in the first year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 靖悼王翊鈴，穆宗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Dao Yi Ling was the Muzong Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Dao (Yi Ling) was the Longqing Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 生未逾年殤，贈藍田王。

translations.literal: He lived less than a year and died in infancy; he was posthumously granted the title Prince of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy before completing his first year and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年追加封謚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing posthumous enfeoffment and title were added.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous enfeoffment and title were added in the first year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 潞簡王翊镠，穆宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Lu Jian Yi Liu was the Muzong Emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu Jian (Yi Liu) was the Longqing Emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年生，生四歲而封。

translations.literal: He was born in the second year of Longqing and was enfeoffed at the age of four.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the second year of Longqing, he was enfeoffed at the age of four.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年之藩衛輝。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he went to his fief at Weihui.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he went to take up his fief at Weihui.

sentences.zh: 初，翊镠以帝母弟居京邸，王店、王莊遍畿內。

translations.literal: At first, because Yi Liu was the emperor's younger maternal brother and lived at the capital residence, princely shops and estates spread throughout the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as the emperor's younger maternal brother living at the capital residence, Yi Liu held princely shops and estates throughout the capital region.

sentences.zh: 比之藩，悉以還官，遂以內臣司之。

translations.literal: When he went to his fief, all were returned to the government, and palace eunuchs were put in charge of them.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to his fief, all were returned to the government and placed under palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 皇店、皇莊自此益侈。

translations.literal: From this time imperial shops and estates grew ever more extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: From then on imperial shops and estates grew ever more extravagant.

sentences.zh: 翊镠居藩，多請贍田、食鹽，無不應者。

translations.literal: While Yi Liu resided in his fief, he frequently requested maintenance lands and salt rations, and none of his requests went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: While residing in his fief, Yi Liu frequently requested maintenance lands and salt rations, and every request was granted.

sentences.zh: 其後福藩遂緣為故事。

translations.literal: Afterward the Prince of Fu followed this as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Prince of Fu took this as precedent.

sentences.zh: 明初，親王歲祿外，量給草場牧地，間有以廢壤河灘請者，多不及千頃。

translations.literal: In the early Ming, apart from the princes' annual stipends, pasturelands were allotted in measured amounts; occasionally requests were made for waste land or river flats, but these usually amounted to less than a thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Ming, apart from princely annual stipends, pasturelands were allotted in measured amounts; occasional requests for waste land or river flats rarely exceeded a thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 部臣得執奏，不盡從也。

translations.literal: Ministry officials could remonstrate and memorialize, and the throne did not always accede.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials could remonstrate in memorials, and the throne did not always comply.

sentences.zh: 景王就藩時，賜予概裁省。

translations.literal: When Prince Jing went to his fief, grants were generally cut back.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jing went to his fief, grants were generally reduced.

sentences.zh: 楚地曠，多閑田，詔悉予之。

translations.literal: The lands of Chu were broad and had much idle farmland; an edict granted all of it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chu had vast tracts of idle farmland, and an edict granted all of it to him.

sentences.zh: 景藩除，潞得景故籍田，多至四萬頃，部臣無以難。

translations.literal: When the Jing princely establishment was abolished, Lu received the Jing prince's former registered lands, amounting to as many as forty thousand qing; ministry officials had no grounds to object.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing princely line was abolished, Lu received the former Jing prince's registered lands — as many as forty thousand qing — and ministry officials had no grounds to object.

sentences.zh: 至福王常洵之國，版籍更定，民力益絀，尺寸皆奪之民間，海內騷然。

translations.literal: By the time Prince Fu Chang Xun went to his fief, land registers were redrawn, the people's strength was further exhausted, every inch was seized from the populace, and the realm was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Prince Fu (Chang Xun) went to his fief, land registers were redrawn, the people's resources were further drained, every scrap of land was seized from commoners, and the realm was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 論者推原事始，頗以翊镠為口實雲。

translations.literal: Commentators tracing the origin of the matter often cited Yi Liu as the starting point.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators tracing the matter to its origins often pointed to Yi Liu as the precedent.

sentences.zh: 翊镠好文，性勤飭，恒以歲入輸之朝，助工助邊無所惜，帝益善之。

translations.literal: Yi Liu loved literature and was by nature diligent and disciplined; he constantly sent his annual income to the court and spared nothing in aiding public works and the frontier, and the emperor thought all the more highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Liu loved literature and was diligent by nature; he regularly sent his annual income to court and spared nothing for public works and frontier defense, and the emperor thought all the more highly of him.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，皇太后哀問至，翊镠悲慟廢寢食，未幾薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, when news came of the empress dowager's death, Yi Liu grieved so deeply that he stopped eating and sleeping, and soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, when news of the empress dowager's death arrived, Yi Liu grieved so deeply that he stopped eating and sleeping, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 世子常淓幼，母妃李氐理藩事。

translations.literal: The heir Chang Fen was young, and his mother, Consort Li, administered princely affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The heir Chang Fen was still young, and his mother Consort Li administered princely affairs.

sentences.zh: 時福王奏請，輒取中旨，帝於王妃奏，亦從中下，示無異同。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Fu's petitions always received direct edicts from the inner court; when the princess consort submitted memorials, the emperor likewise issued orders from within, showing no difference in treatment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Fu's petitions always received direct edicts from the inner court; the princess consort's memorials likewise received orders from within, showing no difference in treatment.

sentences.zh: 部臣言：「王妃奏陳四事，如軍校月糧之當給發，義和店之預防侵奪，義所當許；

translations.literal: Ministry officials said: "In the four matters the princess consort memorialized — such as the proper disbursement of monthly rations for military officers and soldiers, and preventing encroachment on Yihe Shop — what is right ought to be granted;
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials said, "Of the four matters the princess consort raised — such as properly disbursing monthly rations for military officers and soldiers and preventing encroachment on Yihe Shop — some ought rightly to be granted;

sentences.zh: 至歲祿之欲先給，王莊之欲更設，則不當許。

translations.literal: but as for seeking advance payment of the annual stipend and establishing additional princely estates, these ought not to be granted.
translations.idiomatic: but advance payment of the annual stipend and establishing additional princely estates ought not to be granted.

sentences.zh: 且於王無絲豪益，徒令邸中人日魚肉小民，飽私囊。

translations.literal: Moreover they would bring the prince not the slightest benefit, but would only allow those in the residence daily to prey on common people and fill their private purses.
translations.idiomatic: They would bring the prince no benefit at all, but would only let those in the residence prey on common people day after day and fill their private purses.

sentences.zh: 將來本支千億，請索日頻，盡天府之版章，給王邸而不足也。」

translations.literal: In the future, as the princely line branches into thousands and tens of thousands, requests will grow daily in frequency; even exhausting the land registers of the realm would not suffice to supply the princely residence."
translations.idiomatic: As the princely line branches into countless households, requests will grow ever more frequent; even exhausting the realm's land registers would not suffice to supply the princely residence."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，常淓嗣。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year Chang Fen succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year Chang Fen succeeded to the princely title.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，流賊擾秦、晉、河北。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign, roving bandits ravaged Qin, Jin, and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign, roving bandits ravaged Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 常淓疏告急，言：「衛輝城卑土惡，請選護衛三千人助守，捐歲入萬金資餉，不煩司農。」

translations.literal: Chang Fen memorialized in alarm, saying: "Weihui's walls are low and its soil poor; I request that three thousand guards be selected to help defend it, and I will donate ten thousand taels of my annual income for rations, without troubling the Ministry of Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: Chang Fen memorialized in alarm, saying, "Weihui's walls are low and its soil poor; I request three thousand guards to help defend it and will donate ten thousand taels of my annual income for rations, without troubling the Ministry of Revenue."

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: The court commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him.

sentences.zh: 盜發王妃冢，常淓上言：「賊延蔓漸及江北，鳳、泗陵寢可虞，宜早行剿滅。」

translations.literal: When bandits opened the princess consort's tomb, Chang Fen memorialized: "The bandits are spreading and gradually reaching the north of the Yangzi; the tombs at Feng and Si are at risk — suppression ought to be carried out early."
translations.idiomatic: When bandits opened the princess consort's tomb, Chang Fen memorialized, "The bandits are spreading toward the north of the Yangzi; the tombs at Feng and Si are at risk — they should be suppressed at once."

sentences.zh: 時諸藩中能急國難者，惟周、潞二王雲。

translations.literal: At the time, among all the princes who could urgently respond to the national crisis, only the princes of Zhou and Lu were such.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, among all the princes who urgently responded to the national crisis, only the princes of Zhou and Lu did so.

sentences.zh: 後賊躪中州，常淓流寓於杭。

translations.literal: Later, when bandits overran the central provinces, Chang Fen took refuge in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when bandits overran the central provinces, Chang Fen took refuge in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 順治二年六月降於我大清。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi he surrendered to Our Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi he surrendered to the Great Qing.

sentences.zh: 神宗八子。

translations.literal: The Shenzong Emperor had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Wanli Emperor had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 王太后生光宗。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wang bore the Guangzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang bore the Taichang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 鄭貴妃生福王常洵、沅王常治。

translations.literal: Consort Zheng the Noble Consort bore Prince Fu Chang Xun and Prince Yuan Chang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zheng bore Prince Fu (Chang Xun) and Prince Yuan (Chang Zhi).

sentences.zh: 周端妃生瑞王常浩。

translations.literal: Consort Zhou Duan bore Prince Rui Chang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhou Duan bore Prince Rui (Chang Hao).

sentences.zh: 李貴妃生惠王常潤、桂王常瀛。

translations.literal: Consort Li the Noble Consort bore Prince Hui Chang Run and Prince Gui Chang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li bore Prince Hui (Chang Run) and Prince Gui (Chang Ying).

sentences.zh: 其邠王常漵、永思王常溥，母氏無考。

translations.literal: As for Prince Bin Chang Xu and Prince Yong Si Chang Pu, their mothers are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bin (Chang Xu) and Prince Yong Si (Chang Pu)'s mothers are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 邠哀王常漵，神宗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Bin Ai Chang Xu was the Shenzong Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Bin Ai (Chang Xu) was the Wanli Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 生一歲殤。

translations.literal: He lived one year and died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: He lived one year before dying in infancy.

sentences.zh: 福恭王常洵，神宗第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Fu Gong Chang Xun was the Shenzong Emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu Gong (Chang Xun) was the Wanli Emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 初，王皇后無子，王妃生長子，是為光宗。

translations.literal: At first Empress Wang had no sons; the imperial consort bore the eldest son, who became the Guangzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At first Empress Wang had no sons; the imperial consort bore the eldest son, who became the Taichang Emperor.

sentences.zh: 常洵次之，母鄭貴妃最幸。

translations.literal: Chang Xun was next; his mother Consort Zheng was the most favored.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xun was next in line; his mother Consort Zheng was the emperor's favorite.

sentences.zh: 帝久不立太子，中外疑貴妃謀立己子，交章言其事，竄謫相踵，而言者不止。

translations.literal: The emperor for a long time did not establish a crown prince; inside and outside the court suspected the noble consort plotted to install her own son; memorials on the matter piled up one after another, and those who spoke were demoted and exiled in succession, yet the remonstrances did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: For a long time the Wanli Emperor did not name a crown prince. Court and country alike suspected that the favorite consort meant to put her own son on the throne. Memorial after memorial pressed the issue; officials who spoke up were banished in droves, yet the protests never stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝深厭苦之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply hated and was wearied by it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to loathe the controversy.

sentences.zh: 二十九年始立光宗為太子，而封常洵福王，婚費至三十萬，營洛陽邸第至二十八萬，十倍常制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he finally established the Guangzong Emperor as crown prince, while enfeoffing Chang Xun as Prince of Fu; wedding expenses reached three hundred thousand, and building the Luoyang residence reached two hundred eighty thousand—ten times the usual scale.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the twenty-ninth year of his reign did he finally make the Taichang Emperor heir apparent and enfeoff Chang Xun as Prince of Fu. The wedding cost three hundred thousand taels, and the Luoyang mansion cost two hundred eighty thousand—ten times the normal allotment.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請王之藩者數十百奏。

translations.literal: Court officials requesting the prince go to his fief submitted dozens or hundreds of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens upon dozens of memorials from court officials urged the prince to go to his fief.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 至四十二年，始令就藩。

translations.literal: It was not until the forty-second year that he was finally ordered to take up his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the forty-second year was he at last ordered to go to his fief.

sentences.zh: 先是，海內全盛，帝所遣稅使、礦使遍天下，月有進奉，明珠異寶文毳錦綺山積，他搜括贏羨億萬計。

translations.literal: Before this the realm was in full prosperity; tax commissioners and mining commissioners dispatched by the emperor covered the land; each month there were tribute submissions; pearls, rare treasures, fine furs, and brocades piled like mountains; other exactions and surpluses amounted to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the empire had been at its height. Tax and mining commissioners sent by the emperor ranged across the land, and every month fresh tribute arrived. Pearls, curios, fine furs, and brocades stacked up like hills; other levies and surpluses ran into the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 至是多以資常洵。

translations.literal: By then most of it was used to support Chang Xun.
translations.idiomatic: By this time most of those riches were being channeled to Chang Xun.

sentences.zh: 臨行出宮門，召還數四，期以三歲一入朝。

translations.literal: When about to depart and leaving the palace gate, he was summoned back again and again; it was fixed that he would enter court once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure he passed the palace gate, was called back repeatedly, and was granted an audience at court once every three years.

sentences.zh: 下詔賜莊田四萬頃。

translations.literal: An edict was issued granting forty thousand qing of estate lands.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him forty thousand qing of estate land.

sentences.zh: 所司力爭，常洵亦奏辭，得減半。

translations.literal: The responsible offices vigorously contested it; Chang Xun also submitted a memorial declining, and the grant was reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible agencies protested vigorously; Chang Xun too memorialized to decline, and the grant was cut in half.

sentences.zh: 中州腴土不足，取山東、湖廣田益之。

translations.literal: Fertile land in the Central Plains was insufficient, so fields from Shandong and Huguang were taken to supplement it.
translations.idiomatic: Because fertile land in the Central Plains was not enough, fields from Shandong and Huguang were added to make up the total.

sentences.zh: 又奏乞故大學士張居正所沒產，及江都至太平沿江荻洲雜稅，並四川鹽井榷茶銀以自益。

translations.literal: He further memorialized requesting the confiscated property of the former Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng, miscellaneous taxes from reed marshes along the Yangtze from Jiangdu to Taiping, and revenues from Sichuan salt wells and tea monopolies to enrich himself.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for the confiscated estates of the late Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng, miscellaneous taxes on riverside reed lands from Jiangdu to Taiping, and the silver from Sichuan salt wells and tea monopolies—all to pad his own income.

sentences.zh: 伴讀、承奉諸官，假履畝為名，乘傳出入河南北、齊、楚間，所至騷動。

translations.literal: Tutor-companions, palace attendants, and other officials, on the pretext of surveying fields, traveled by relay post between Henan, the north, Qi, and Chu, causing disturbances wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: Tutors, palace attendants, and other staff, under the pretext of measuring fields, rode the relay posts through Henan, the north, Qi, and Chu, stirring up trouble wherever they appeared.

sentences.zh: 又請淮鹽千三百引，設店洛陽與民市。

translations.literal: He also requested thirteen hundred Huai salt certificates and set up shops in Luoyang to trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: He further requested thirteen hundred Huai salt certificates and opened shops in Luoyang to sell salt to the public.

sentences.zh: 中使至淮、揚支鹽，乾沒要求輒數倍。

translations.literal: Eunuch commissioners went to Huai and Yang to draw salt; embezzlement and extortion often amounted to several times the proper sum.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuch envoys went to Huai and Yang to collect salt, their embezzlement and demands routinely ran to several times the proper amount.

sentences.zh: 而中州舊食河東鹽，以改食淮鹽故，禁非王肆所出不得鬻，河東引遏不行，邊餉由此絀。

translations.literal: The Central Plains had formerly consumed Hedong salt; because they switched to Huai salt, it was forbidden to sell any not issued from the prince's shops; Hedong certificates were blocked and could not circulate, and frontier pay was thereby reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains had long used Hedong salt, but after the switch to Huai salt only salt from the prince's shops could be sold. Hedong certificates were blocked from circulation, and frontier supplies suffered as a result.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請改給王鹽於河東，且無與民市。

translations.literal: Court officials requested that the prince's salt allotment be changed to Hedong and that he not trade with the people.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials asked that the prince's salt be supplied from Hedong instead and that he not sell to the public.

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 帝深居久，群臣章奏率不省。

translations.literal: The emperor had long lived in seclusion; memorials from officials were generally not reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long withdrawn from court, and officials' memorials usually went unread.

sentences.zh: 獨福藩使通籍中左門，一日數請，朝上夕報可。

translations.literal: Only the Prince of Fu's envoys had registered access through the Central Left Gate; requests several times a day were submitted in the morning and approved by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Prince of Fu's messengers held registered access at the Central Left Gate; they petitioned several times a day and received approval by evening.

sentences.zh: 四方奸人亡命，探風旨，走利如鶩。

translations.literal: Rogues and fugitives from the four directions, gauging the emperor's intentions, flocked to profit like ducks to water.
translations.idiomatic: Scoundrels and fugitives from every quarter, reading the court's mood, rushed to turn a profit like ducks to a pond.

sentences.zh: 如是者終萬歷之世。

translations.literal: Such was the case throughout the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: This went on for the rest of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 及崇禎時，常洵地近屬尊，朝廷尊禮之。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen era, because Chang Xun was a close imperial relative and held high rank, the court honored him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era Chang Xun, as a close imperial kinsman of high standing, was treated with special honor by the court.

sentences.zh: 常洵日閉閣飲醇酒，所好惟婦女倡樂。

translations.literal: Chang Xun daily shut himself in his chambers drinking fine wine; his only pleasures were women and musical entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xun spent his days behind closed doors drinking fine wine; his only interests were women and song.

sentences.zh: 秦中流賊起，河南大旱蝗，人相食，民間藉藉，謂先帝耗天下以肥王，洛陽富於大內。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in the Qin region; Henan suffered great drought and locusts; people ate one another; rumors spread among the populace that the previous emperor had drained the realm to enrich the prince, and that Luoyang was wealthier than the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits broke out in the Qin region; Henan was stricken by drought and locusts, and people resorted to cannibalism. Rumors ran wild that the late Wanli Emperor had drained the empire to fatten the prince, and that Luoyang was richer than the imperial palace.

sentences.zh: 援兵過洛者，喧言：「王府金錢百萬，而令吾輩枵腹死賊手。」

translations.literal: Relief troops passing through Luoyang shouted aloud: "The princely residence has millions in gold and cash, yet they leave us starving to die at the bandits' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops passing through Luoyang cried out: "The princely mansion holds millions in gold and silver, yet we are left to starve and die at the bandits' hands!

sentences.zh: 南京兵部尚書呂維祺方家居，聞之懼，以利害告常洵，不為意。

translations.literal: Lü Weiji, former Minister of War at Nanjing, was at home when he heard this and was afraid; he explained the danger to Chang Xun, who paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Weiji, the former Nanjing Minister of War, was living at home when he heard this and was alarmed. He explained the danger to Chang Xun, who took no notice.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，李自成連舀永寧、宜陽。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year, Li Zicheng successively captured Yongning and Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year, Li Zicheng successively captured Yongning and Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，參政王胤昌帥眾警備，總兵官王紹禹，副將劉見義、羅泰各引兵至。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, Vice Commissioner Wang Yinchang led troops on alert; Commander-in-Chief Wang Shaoyu and Vice Generals Liu Jianyi and Luo Tai each led troops there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, Vice Commissioner Wang Yinchang mustered troops on alert, while Commander Wang Shaoyu and Vice Generals Liu Jianyi and Luo Tai each marched in with their forces.

sentences.zh: 常洵召三將入，賜宴加禮。

translations.literal: Chang Xun summoned the three generals in, feasted them, and treated them with added honor.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xun summoned the three generals, feasted them, and showed them special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 越數日，賊大至，攻城。

translations.literal: A few days later the bandits arrived in force and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the rebels arrived in strength and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 常洵出千金募勇士，縋而出，用矛入賊營，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: Chang Xun offered a thousand taels of gold to recruit brave men; they were lowered by rope over the wall, entered the bandit camp with spears, and the bandits withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xun offered a thousand taels of gold to recruit brave fighters. They were lowered by rope over the wall, spear in hand, raided the rebel camp, and drove the enemy back somewhat.

sentences.zh: 夜半，紹禹親軍從城上呼賊相笑語，揮刀殺守堞者，燒城樓，開北門納賊。

translations.literal: At midnight Wang Shaoyu's personal guard called out to the bandits from the ramparts and bantered with them; they swung their blades and killed the defenders on the parapet, burned the gate tower, opened the north gate, and admitted the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Wang Shaoyu's personal troops called down to the rebels from the wall and joked with them, then slashed the defenders on the parapet, burned the gate tower, opened the north gate, and let the rebels in.

sentences.zh: 常洵縋城出，匿迎恩寺。

translations.literal: Chang Xun was lowered by rope over the wall and fled, hiding at Ying'en Monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xun was lowered by rope over the wall and took refuge at Ying'en Monastery.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賊跡而執之，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits tracked him down and seized him, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels tracked him down, seized him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 兩承奉伏屍哭，賊捽之去。

translations.literal: Two palace attendants prostrated themselves weeping over the corpse; the bandits dragged them away.
translations.idiomatic: Two palace attendants threw themselves on the body and wept; the rebels dragged them away.

sentences.zh: 承奉呼曰：「王死某不願生，乞一棺收王骨，棆粉無所恨。」

translations.literal: An attendant cried out: "The prince is dead—I do not wish to live. I beg one coffin to collect the prince's bones; to be ground to powder I would have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: One attendant cried out: "The prince is dead—I do not wish to live. Grant me a coffin to gather his bones, and I would be ground to dust without regret.

sentences.zh: 賊義而許之。

translations.literal: The bandits were moved and granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, the rebels agreed.

sentences.zh: 桐棺一寸，載以斷車，兩人即其旁自縊死。

translations.literal: A paulownia coffin one inch thick was placed on a broken cart; the two men hanged themselves beside it.
translations.idiomatic: A thin paulownia coffin was placed on a broken cart, and the two men hanged themselves beside it.

sentences.zh: 王妃鄒氏及世子由崧走懷慶。

translations.literal: Consort Zou and the heir Zhu Yousong fled to Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zou and the heir Zhu Yousong fled to Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 賊火王宮，三日不絕。

translations.literal: The bandits set fire to the princely palace; the flames burned for three days without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels torched the princely palace, and the fire burned for three days without stopping.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝震悼，輟朝三日，令河南有司改殯。

translations.literal: When word reached the emperor, he was shaken with grief, suspended court for three days, and ordered Henan officials to rebury the remains properly.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the Chongzhen Emperor, he was stricken with grief, suspended court for three days, and ordered the Henan authorities to give the prince a proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 十六年秋七月，由崧襲封，帝親擇宮中寶玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the sixteenth year, Zhu Yousong inherited the title; the emperor personally chose a palace jade belt and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn in the sixteenth year Zhu Yousong succeeded to the title, and the emperor personally selected a jade belt from the palace stores and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，京師失守，由崧與潞王常淓俱避賊至淮安。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year the capital fell; Zhu Yousong and Prince of Lu Chang Fang both fled the bandits to Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year the capital fell. Zhu Yousong and Prince of Lu Chang Fang both fled the rebels to Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 四月，鳳陽總督馬士英等迎由崧入南京。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Fengyang Grand Coordinator Ma Shiying and others welcomed Zhu Yousong into Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Fengyang Grand Coordinator Ma Shiying and others welcomed Zhu Yousong into Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 五月庚寅，稱監國。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the fifth month, he was proclaimed regent.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the fifth month he assumed the regency.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書史可法、戶部尚書高弘圖及士英俱為大學士，士英仍督鳳陽軍務。

translations.literal: Minister of War Shi Kefa, Minister of Revenue Gao Hongtu, and Ma Shiying were all appointed Grand Secretaries; Ma Shiying continued to oversee Fengyang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa, Minister of War, Gao Hongtu, Minister of Revenue, and Ma Shiying were all made Grand Secretaries; Ma Shiying continued to direct military affairs at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 壬寅自立於南京，偽號弘光。

translations.literal: On the renyin day he proclaimed himself emperor at Nanjing and took the rebel title Hongguang.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day he declared himself emperor at Nanjing and proclaimed the era name Hongguang.

sentences.zh: 史可法督師江北。

translations.literal: Shi Kefa directed armies north of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kefa took command of the armies north of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 召士英入，分淮、揚、鳳、廬為四鎮，以總兵官黃得功、劉良佐、劉澤清、高傑領之。

translations.literal: Ma Shiying was summoned to enter; Huai, Yang, Feng, and Lu were divided into four defense zones, commanded by Commanders-in-Chief Huang Degong, Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie respectively.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiying was summoned to court. Huai, Yang, Feng, and Lu were divided into four military zones under the commanders Huang Degong, Liu Liangzuo, Liu Zeqing, and Gao Jie.

sentences.zh: 由崧性闇弱，湛於酒色聲伎，委任士英及士英黨阮大鋮，擢至兵部尚書，巡閱江防。

translations.literal: Zhu Yousong's nature was dim and weak; he was sunk in wine, women, and performers; he entrusted power to Ma Shiying and Ma's ally Ruan Dacheng, who was promoted to Minister of War to inspect river defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yousong was dull and weak, lost in wine, women, and entertainers. He put his trust in Ma Shiying and Ma's ally Ruan Dacheng, whom he promoted to Minister of War to oversee river defenses.

sentences.zh: 二人日以鬻官爵、報私憾為事。

translations.literal: The two daily sold offices and titles and settled private scores.
translations.idiomatic: The two spent their days selling offices and settling private grudges.

sentences.zh: 事詳諸臣傳中。

translations.literal: The details are given in the biographies of the various officials.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the biographies of the various officials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有王之明者，詐稱莊烈帝太子，下之獄。

translations.literal: Before long a man named Wang Zhiming falsely claimed to be the Chongzhen Emperor's crown prince and was thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a man named Wang Zhiming falsely claimed to be the crown prince of the Chongzhen Emperor and was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 又有婦童氏，自稱由崧妃，亦下獄。

translations.literal: There was also a woman surnamed Tong who claimed to be Zhu Yousong's consort; she too was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: A woman surnamed Tong also claimed to be Zhu Yousong's consort and was imprisoned as well.

sentences.zh: 於是中外嘩然。

translations.literal: At this inside and outside the court erupted in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At this court and country alike erupted in uproar.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，寧南侯左良玉舉兵武昌，以救太子誅士英為名，順流東下。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, Marquis of Ningnan Zuo Liangyu raised troops at Wuchang, claiming to rescue the crown prince and execute Ma Shiying, and marched downstream to the east.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year Marquis of Ningnan Zuo Liangyu raised troops at Wuchang, claiming he would rescue the crown prince and execute Ma Shiying, and marched downstream.

sentences.zh: 阮大鋮、黃得功等帥師禦之。

translations.literal: Ruan Dacheng, Huang Degong, and others led armies to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dacheng, Huang Degong, and others led troops to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 而我大清兵以是年五月己丑渡江。

translations.literal: And our Great Qing army crossed the Yangtze on the jichou day of the fifth month that year.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, on the jichou day of the fifth month, the Great Qing army crossed the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 辛卯夜，由崧走太平，蓋趨得功軍也。

translations.literal: On the night of the xinmao day Zhu Yousong fled to Taiping—intending to reach Huang Degong's army.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the xinmao day Zhu Yousong fled to Taiping, apparently aiming to join Huang Degong's army.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，士英挾由崧母妃奔杭州。

translations.literal: On the renchen day Ma Shiying took Zhu Yousong's mother and consort and fled to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day Ma Shiying fled to Hangzhou with Zhu Yousong's mother and consort.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，由崧至蕪湖。

translations.literal: On the guisi day Zhu Yousong reached Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day Zhu Yousong reached Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 丙申，大兵至南京城北，文武官出降。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day the great army reached north of Nanjing; civil and military officials came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day the Qing army reached the north of Nanjing, and civil and military officials came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 丙午，執由崧至南京。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day Zhu Yousong was seized and brought to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day Zhu Yousong was captured and brought to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 九月甲寅，以歸京師。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the ninth month he was sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day of the ninth month he was sent back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 沅懷王常治，神宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan Huai Chang Zhi was the Shenzong Emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Huai (Chang Zhi) was the Wanli Emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 生一歲殤。

translations.literal: He lived one year and died in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: He lived one year before dying in infancy.

sentences.zh: 瑞王常浩，神宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Rui Chang Hao was the Shenzong Emperor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui (Chang Hao) was the Wanli Emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初，太子未立，有三王並封之旨，蓋謂光宗、福王及常浩也。

translations.literal: At first, before the crown prince was appointed, there was an edict to enfeoff three princes together—meaning the Guangzong Emperor, the Prince of Fu, and Chang Hao.
translations.idiomatic: At first, before a crown prince had been named, there was an edict to enfeoff three princes at once—the Taichang Emperor, the Prince of Fu, and Chang Hao.

sentences.zh: 尋以群臣爭，遂寢。

translations.literal: Soon, because officials contested it, the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, after officials protested, the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，東宮立，與福、惠、桂三王同日封。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Eastern Palace was established, and together with the Princes of Fu, Hui, and Gui he was enfeoffed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the heir apparent was installed, and on the same day the Princes of Fu, Hui, and Gui were enfeoffed along with him.

sentences.zh: 常洵以長，先之藩。

translations.literal: Chang Xun, being the eldest, went to his fief first.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xun, as the eldest, went to his fief first.

sentences.zh: 常浩年已二十有五，尚末選婚。

translations.literal: Chang Hao was already twenty-five and still had not had a consort selected for marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Hao was already twenty-five and still had no consort chosen for him.

sentences.zh: 群臣交章言，率不報，而日索部帑為婚費，贏十八萬，藏宮中，且言冠服不能備。

translations.literal: Officials submitted memorials one after another; generally there was no response, yet daily they demanded funds from the ministry for wedding expenses, amassed one hundred eighty thousand, hoarded them in the palace, and claimed even ceremonial robes could not be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Officials submitted memorial after memorial, but generally received no answer, while the palace daily demanded ministry funds for wedding expenses, amassed one hundred eighty thousand taels, hoarded them inside the palace, and claimed even ceremonial robes could not be readied.

sentences.zh: 天啟七年之藩漢中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Tianqi reign he went to his fief at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Tianqi reign he went to his fief at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，流寇劇，封地當賊沖。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen era roving bandits were fierce; his fief lay in their path.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen era banditry was severe, and his fief lay directly in the rebels' path.

sentences.zh: 七年上書言：「臣托先帝骨肉，獲奉西藩，未期年而寇至。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject relies on the former emperor's kinship and has been granted the western fief; before a full year had passed bandits arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he memorialized: "Your subject, trusting in the late emperor's kinship, was granted a fief in the west; before a full year had passed bandits arrived.

sentences.zh: 比西賊再渡河，闌入漢興，破洵陽，逼興安，紫陽、平利、白河相繼陷沒。

translations.literal: Recently western bandits crossed the river again, burst into Hanxing, took Xunyang, pressed toward Xing'an; Ziyang, Pingli, and Baihe fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Recently western rebels crossed the river again, broke into Hanxing, took Xunyang, and pressed on Xing'an; Ziyang, Pingli, and Baihe fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 督臣洪承疇單騎裹甲出入萬山，賊始敗遁。

translations.literal: Governor Hong Chengchou rode alone in armor through the Wan Mountains, and only then were the bandits defeated and put to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Hong Chengchou rode alone in armor through the Wan Mountains before the rebels were finally beaten and driven off.

sentences.zh: 臣捐犒軍振饑銀七千余兩。

translations.literal: Your subject contributed over seven thousand taels of silver to reward the army and relieve famine.
translations.idiomatic: I contributed more than seven thousand taels of silver to reward the troops and relieve famine.

sentences.zh: 此時撫臣練國事移兵商、洛，按臣範復粹馳赴漢中，近境稍寧。

translations.literal: At this time Governor Lian Guoshi moved troops to Shang and Luo; Regional Inspector Fan Fuchun rushed to Hanzhong, and the nearby region was somewhat quiet.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Governor Lian Guoshi shifted troops to Shang and Luo, and Regional Inspector Fan Fuchun hurried to Hanzhong; the nearby region grew somewhat calm.

sentences.zh: 既而鳳縣再陷，蜀賊入秦州，楚賊上興安。

translations.literal: Then Feng County fell again; Shu bandits entered Qinzhou; Chu bandits marched on Xing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Then Feng County fell again, Shu rebels entered Qinzhou, and Chu rebels advanced on Xing'an.

sentences.zh: 六月遂犯郡界，幸諸將憑江力拒，賊方稍退。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they then invaded the prefectural boundary; fortunately the generals held them at the river with all their strength, and the bandits withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they invaded the prefectural border; fortunately the generals held the river line with all their strength and the rebels withdrew somewhat.

sentences.zh: 臣在萬山絕谷中，賊四面至，覆亡無日。

translations.literal: Your subject was in deep mountain valleys; bandits came from all four sides; destruction seemed imminent.
translations.idiomatic: I was trapped in deep mountain valleys with rebels closing in from every side; ruin seemed only days away.

sentences.zh: 臣肺腑至親，藩封最僻，而於寇盜至迫，惟陛下哀憐。」

translations.literal: Your subject is the emperor's closest kin, my fief the most remote, yet bandits press upon me—I beg Your Majesty's pity.
translations.idiomatic: I am Your Majesty's closest kin, yet my fief is the most remote, and bandits press hard upon me—I beg Your Majesty's compassion.

sentences.zh: 常浩在宮中，衣服禮秩降等，好佛不近女色。

translations.literal: Chang Hao in the palace had reduced raiment and ceremonial rank, devoted himself to Buddhism, and did not consort with women.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Hao, while at court, wore reduced dress and accepted lowered ceremonial rank. He devoted himself to Buddhism and shunned women.

sentences.zh: 及寇逼秦中，將吏不能救，乞師於蜀。

translations.literal: When bandits pressed on Qinzhong and local officers could not save him, he begged troops from Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits closed in on Qinzhong and local officers could not save him, he begged Shu for troops.

sentences.zh: 總兵官侯良柱援之，遂奔重慶。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Hou Liangzhu came to his aid, and he then fled to Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Hou Liangzhu came to his aid, and he fled to Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 隴西士大夫多挈家以從。

translations.literal: Many gentry families of Longxi took their households and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Many gentry families from Longxi took their households and followed him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，張獻忠陷重慶，被執，遇害。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhang Xianzhong took Chongqing; Chang Hao was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Zhang Xianzhong captured Chongqing; Chang Hao was seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 時天無雲而雷者三，從死者甚眾。

translations.literal: At the time thunder pealed three times though the sky was cloudless; many followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder rolled three times though the sky was clear, and many died with him.

sentences.zh: 惠王常潤，神宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Hui Chang Run was the Shenzong Emperor's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui (Chang Run) was the Wanli Emperor's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 福王之藩，內廷蓄積為空。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu went to his fief, the inner palace's accumulated stores were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu went to his fief, the inner palace's accumulated stores were emptied.

sentences.zh: 中官藉諸王冠婚，索部帑以實宮中，所需輒數十萬，珠寶稱是。

translations.literal: Eunuchs, citing princes' investiture and weddings, demanded ministry funds to fill the palace; each time needs ran to hundreds of thousands, with jewels in like measure.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs, citing princes' investitures and weddings, demanded ministry funds to replenish the palace; each request ran to hundreds of thousands of taels, with jewels to match.

sentences.zh: 戶部不能給。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue could not supply them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue could not meet the demand.

sentences.zh: 常潤與弟常瀛年二十，皆未選婚。

translations.literal: Chang Run and his younger brother Chang Ying were both twenty and still had no consorts chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Run and his younger brother Chang Ying were both twenty and still had no consorts chosen.

sentences.zh: 其後兵事亟，始滅殺成禮。

translations.literal: Afterward military affairs grew urgent and the ceremonies were finally cut back to the minimum.
translations.idiomatic: Only when military affairs grew urgent were the ceremonies finally stripped to the bare minimum.

sentences.zh: 天啟七年之藩荊州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Tianqi reign he went to his fief at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Tianqi reign he went to his fief at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年十二月，李自成再破夷陵、荊門，常潤走湘潭，自成入荊州據之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fifteenth year of the Chongzhen reign, Li Zicheng again took Yiling and Jingmen; Chang Run fled to Xiangtan; Zicheng entered Jingzhou and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fifteenth year of the Chongzhen reign, Li Zicheng again captured Yiling and Jingmen. Chang Run fled to Xiangtan while Zicheng entered Jingzhou and took possession of it.

sentences.zh: 常潤之渡湘也，遇風於陵陽磯，宮人多漂沒，身僅以免，就吉王於長沙。

translations.literal: When Chang Run was crossing the Xiang, he met wind at Lingyang Ji; many palace women were washed away and drowned; he himself barely escaped, and went to join the Prince of Ji at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang Run was crossing the Xiang River, his party was struck by a storm at Lingyang Ji. Many palace women were swept away and drowned; he himself barely escaped with his life and went to join the Prince of Ji at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 十六年八月，張獻忠陷長沙，常潤走衡州，就桂王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year, Zhang Xianzhong took Changsha; Chang Run fled to Hengzhou and joined the Prince of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the sixteenth year of the Chongzhen reign, Zhang Xianzhong captured Changsha. Chang Run fled to Hengzhou and joined the Prince of Gui.

sentences.zh: 衡州繼陷，與吉王、桂王走永州。

translations.literal: Hengzhou soon fell as well; together with the Princes of Ji and Gui he fled to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hengzhou soon fell as well, and together with the Princes of Ji and Gui he fled to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史劉熙祚遣人護三王入廣西，以身當賊。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Liu Xizuo sent men to escort the three princes into Guangxi, taking the enemy on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Liu Xizuo sent men to escort the three princes into Guangxi while he himself stood in the enemy's path.

sentences.zh: 永州陷，熙祚死之。

translations.literal: When Yongzhou fell, Xizuo died there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongzhou fell, Xizuo died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 桂端王常瀛，神宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Duan of Gui, Chang Ying, was the Shenzong Emperor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan of Gui (Chang Ying) was the Wanli Emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 天啟七年之藩衡州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Tianqi reign he went to his fief at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Tianqi reign he went to his fief at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年，衡州陷，與吉、惠二王同走廣西，居梧州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of the Chongzhen reign, Hengzhou fell; together with the Princes of Ji and Hui he fled to Guangxi and lived at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of the Chongzhen reign, Hengzhou fell. Together with the Princes of Ji and Hui he fled to Guangxi and took up residence at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 世子已先卒，次子安仁王由𣜬亦未幾卒。

translations.literal: The heir apparent had already died beforehand; the second son, Prince Anren You Ai, also died before long.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent had already died beforehand, and the second son, Prince Anren (You Ai), also died before long.

sentences.zh: 次由榔，崇禎時，封永明王。

translations.literal: Next was Youlang, who during the Chongzhen reign was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongming.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Zhu Youlang, who during the Chongzhen reign was enfeoffed as Prince of Yongming.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，由平樂、潯州走桂林。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, he fled from Pinglo and Xunzhou to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year, Zhu Youlang fled from Pinglo and Xunzhou to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 魁楚棄由榔，走岑溪，降於大軍。

translations.literal: Kuitu abandoned Youlang, fled to Cenxi, and surrendered to the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Kuitu abandoned Zhu Youlang, fled to Cenxi, and surrendered to the Great Qing army.

sentences.zh: 既而平樂不守，由榔大恐。

translations.literal: Before long Pinglo could not be held, and Youlang was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Pinglo could no longer be held, and Zhu Youlang was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 會武岡總兵官劉承胤以兵至全州，王坤請赴之。

translations.literal: Just then the Wugang regional commander Liu Chengyin arrived at Quanzhou with troops, and Wang Kun asked to go join him.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Chengyin, regional commander at Wugang, arrived at Quanzhou with troops, and Wang Kun urged going to join him.

sentences.zh: 式耜力諫。

translations.literal: Shi Mi remonstrated with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Shi Mi remonstrated vehemently.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youlang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 乃以式耜及總兵官焦璉留守桂林，封陳邦傳為思恩侯，守昭平，遂趨承胤軍中。

translations.literal: He then left Shi Mi and the regional commander Jiao Lin to hold Guilin, enfeoffed Chen Bangchuan as Marquis of Si'en to guard Zhaoping, and hastened to Chengyin's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Qu Shi Mi and regional commander Jiao Lin to hold Guilin, enfeoffed Chen Bangchuan as Marquis of Si'en to guard Zhaoping, and hastened to Liu Chengyin's camp.

sentences.zh: 三月封承胤安國公，錦衣指揮馬吉翔等為伯。

translations.literal: In the third month he enfeoffed Chengyin as Duke of Anguo and made Brocade Guard commander Ma Jixiang and others counts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he enfeoffed Liu Chengyin as Duke of Anguo and made Brocade Guard commander Ma Jixiang and others counts.

sentences.zh: 承胤挾由榔歸武岡，改曰奉天府，政事皆決焉。

translations.literal: Chengyin took Youlang back to Wugang, renamed it Fengtian Prefecture, and all government affairs were decided there.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chengyin took Zhu Youlang back to Wugang, renamed it Fengtian Prefecture, and all affairs of government were decided there.

sentences.zh: 是時，長沙、衡、永皆不守，湖廣總督何騰蛟與侍郎嚴起恒走白牙市。

translations.literal: At this time Changsha, Heng, and Yong could all no longer be held; Huguang governor-general He Tengjiao and vice minister Yan Qiheng fled to Baiya Market.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Changsha, Hengzhou, and Yongzhou could all no longer be held. Huguang governor-general He Tengjiao and vice minister Yan Qiheng fled to Baiya Market.

sentences.zh: 六月，由榔遣官召騰蛟至，密使除承胤，顧承胤勢盛，騰蛟復還白牙。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Youlang sent an official to summon Tengjiao, secretly intending to remove Chengyin; but seeing Chengyin's power, Tengjiao returned to Baiya.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhu Youlang sent an official to summon He Tengjiao, secretly intending to remove Liu Chengyin; but seeing Chengyin's power, Tengjiao returned to Baiya.

sentences.zh: 大兵由寶慶趨武岡，馬吉翔等挾由榔走靖州，承胤舉城降。

translations.literal: The great army advanced from Baqing toward Wugang; Ma Jixiang and others took Youlang and fled to Jingzhou; Chengyin surrendered the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Qing army advanced from Baqing toward Wugang. Ma Jixiang and others took Zhu Youlang and fled to Jingzhou, while Liu Chengyin surrendered the entire city.

sentences.zh: 由榔又奔柳州。

translations.literal: Youlang fled again to Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youlang fled again to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 道出古泥。

translations.literal: On the road they passed Guni.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they passed through Guni.

sentences.zh: 總兵官侯性、太監龐天壽帥舟師來迎。

translations.literal: Regional commander Hou Xing and eunuch Pang Tianshou led a fleet to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Hou Xing and eunuch Pang Tianshou led a fleet to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 會天雨饑餓，性供帳甚備。

translations.literal: It happened to be raining and there was hunger; Xing's provisions and camp fittings were very complete.
translations.idiomatic: Rain had fallen and there was hunger along the way, but Hou Xing's provisions and camp fittings were abundantly supplied.

sentences.zh: 九月，土舍覃鳴珂作亂，大掠城中，矢及由榔舟。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the native officer Qin Mingke rose in revolt, looted the city on a great scale, and arrows reached Youlang's boat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month native officer Qin Mingke rose in revolt and looted the city on a great scale; arrows even reached Zhu Youlang's boat.

sentences.zh: 先是，大兵趨桂林，焦璉拒守甚力，又廣州有警，大兵東向，桂林稍安。

translations.literal: Earlier the great army had advanced on Guilin; Jiao Lin had resisted and held very firmly; moreover there was an alarm at Guangzhou, the great army turned eastward, and Guilin grew somewhat secure.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Great Qing army had advanced on Guilin, and Jiao Lin had resisted with great tenacity. Moreover, when an alarm arose at Guangzhou, the Great Qing army turned eastward and Guilin grew somewhat secure.

sentences.zh: 既而湖南十三鎮將郝永忠、盧鼎等俱奔赴桂林，騰蛟亦至，與式耜議分地給諸將，使各自為守。

translations.literal: Before long the thirteen garrison generals of Hunan — Hao Yongzhong, Lu Ding, and others — all rushed to Guilin; Tengjiao also arrived, and together with Shi Mi they discussed allotting territories to the various generals so each could hold his own ground.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the thirteen garrison generals of Hunan — Hao Yongzhong, Lu Ding, and others — all rushed to Guilin. He Tengjiao also arrived, and together with Qu Shi Mi they discussed allotting territories to the various generals so that each could hold his own ground.

sentences.zh: 璉已先復陽朔、平樂，陳邦傳復潯州，合兵復梧州，廣西全省略定。

translations.literal: Lin had already recovered Yangshuo and Pinglo; Chen Bangchuan recovered Xunzhou; their combined forces retook Wuzhou, and all of Guangxi was roughly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Lin had already recovered Yangshuo and Pinglo; Chen Bangchuan recovered Xunzhou; their combined forces retook Wuzhou, and all of Guangxi was roughly pacified.

sentences.zh: 十二月，由榔返桂林。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Youlang returned to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhu Youlang returned to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，大兵至靈川，郝永忠潰於興安，奔還，挾由榔走柳州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, the great army reached Lingchuan; Hao Yongzhong was routed at Xing'an, fled back, and took Youlang with him to Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of the Yongli reign, the Great Qing army reached Lingchuan. Hao Yongzhong was routed at Xing'an, fled back, and took Zhu Youlang with him to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大兵攻桂林，式耜、騰蛟拒戰。

translations.literal: The great army attacked Guilin; Shi Mi and Tengjiao resisted in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Qing army attacked Guilin, and Qu Shi Mi and He Tengjiao resisted in battle.

sentences.zh: 時南昌金聲桓等叛，降於由榔。

translations.literal: At the time Jin Shenghuan and others at Nanchang rebelled and surrendered to Youlang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jin Shenghuan and others at Nanchang rebelled and surrendered to Zhu Youlang.

sentences.zh: 八月，由榔至肇慶。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Youlang reached Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhu Youlang reached Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 六年春，大兵下湘潭，何騰蛟死。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, the great army took Xiangtan and He Tengjiao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year of the Yongli reign, the Great Qing army took Xiangtan and He Tengjiao was killed.

sentences.zh: 明年，由榔走梧州。

translations.literal: The following year Youlang fled to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhu Youlang fled to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，大兵入桂林，瞿式耜及總督張同敞死焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year the great army entered Guilin; Qu Shi Mi and governor Zhang Tongchang died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year the Great Qing army entered Guilin, and Qu Shi Mi and governor Zhang Tongchang died there.

sentences.zh: 由榔聞報大懼，自梧州奔南寧。

translations.literal: When Youlang heard the report he was greatly afraid and fled from Wuzhou to Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Youlang heard the report he was stricken with fear and fled from Wuzhou to Nanning.

sentences.zh: 時孫可望已據滇、黔，受封為秦王。

translations.literal: At the time Sun Kewang already held Yunnan and Guizhou and had received investiture as King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sun Kewang already held Yunnan and Guizhou and had received investiture as King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，遣兵來衛，殺嚴起恒等。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he sent troops to guard the court and killed Yan Qiheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year of the Yongli reign he sent troops to guard the court and killed Yan Qiheng and others.

sentences.zh: 九年二月，可望迎由榔入安隆所，改曰安龍府。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year, Kewang welcomed Youlang into Anlong subprefecture and renamed it Anlong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year of the Yongli reign, Sun Kewang welcomed Zhu Youlang into Anlong subprefecture and renamed it Anlong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，日益窮促，聞李定國與可望有隙，遣使密召定國，以兵來迎。

translations.literal: After a long time his situation grew daily more desperate; hearing that Li Dingguo and Kewang were at odds, he secretly sent envoys to summon Dingguo to come with troops to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: As time passed his situation grew daily more desperate. Hearing that Li Dingguo and Sun Kewang were at odds, he secretly sent envoys to summon Dingguo to come with troops and escort him away.

sentences.zh: 馬吉翔黨於可望，偵知之，大學士吳貞毓以下十余人皆被殺。

translations.literal: Ma Jixiang was allied with Kewang; he discovered the plot, and Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and more than ten others were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jixiang was allied with Sun Kewang; he discovered the plot, and Grand Secretary Wu Zhenyu and more than ten others were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 事詳《貞毓傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is told in detail in the "Biography of Zhen Yu."
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recounted at length in the "Biography of Zhen Yu."

sentences.zh: 後二年，李定國敗於新會，將由安隆入滇。

translations.literal: Two years later Li Dingguo was defeated at Xinhui and intended to enter Yunnan from Anlong.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Li Dingguo was defeated at Xinhui and intended to enter Yunnan from Anlong.

sentences.zh: 可望患之，促由榔移貴陽就己。

translations.literal: Kewang was troubled by this and urged Youlang to move to Guiyang to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang was troubled by this and urged Zhu Youlang to move to Guiyang and join him.

sentences.zh: 由榔故遲行。

translations.literal: Youlang deliberately delayed his departure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youlang deliberately delayed his departure.

sentences.zh: 定國至，遂奉由榔由安南衛走雲南，居可望署中，封定國晉王。

translations.literal: When Dingguo arrived, he escorted Youlang from Annan Guard through Yunnan, lodged him in Kewang's headquarters, and enfeoffed Dingguo as King of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Dingguo arrived, he escorted Zhu Youlang from Annan Guard through Yunnan, lodged him in Sun Kewang's headquarters, and enfeoffed Dingguo as King of Jin.

sentences.zh: 可望以妻子在滇，未敢動。

translations.literal: Kewang, because his wife and children were in Yunnan, did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang, because his wife and children were in Yunnan, did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 明年，由榔送其妻子還黔，遂舉兵與定國戰於三岔。

translations.literal: The following year Youlang sent Kewang's wife and children back to Guizhou; Kewang then raised troops and fought Dingguo at Sancha.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhu Youlang sent Sun Kewang's wife and children back to Guizhou. Kewang then raised troops and fought Li Dingguo at Sancha.

sentences.zh: 可望將白文選單騎奔定國軍。

translations.literal: Kewang's general Bai Wenxuan rode alone to Dingguo's army and defected.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang's general Bai Wenxuan rode alone into Li Dingguo's camp and defected.

sentences.zh: 可望敗，挈妻子赴長沙大軍前降。

translations.literal: Kewang was defeated, took his wife and children, and surrendered before the great army at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang was defeated, took his wife and children, and surrendered before the Great Qing army at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，大兵三路入雲南。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, the great army entered Yunnan by three routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year of the Yongli reign, the Great Qing army entered Yunnan by three routes.

sentences.zh: 定國厄雞公背，斷貴州道，別將守七星關，抵生界立營，以牽蜀師。

translations.literal: Dingguo was blocked at Jigongbei, cut the Guizhou road, set another commander to hold Qixing Pass, and established a camp at Shengjie to tie down the Shu column.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo was blocked at Jigongbei, cut the Guizhou road, posted another commander to hold Qixing Pass, and established a camp at Shengjie to tie down the Sichuan column.

sentences.zh: 大兵出遵義，由水西取烏撒，守將棄關走，李定國連敗於安隆，由榔走永昌。

translations.literal: The great army came out of Zunyi, took Wusa by way of Shuixi; the defending commander abandoned the pass and fled; Li Dingguo suffered successive defeats at Anlong; Youlang fled to Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Qing army came out of Zunyi and took Wusa by way of Shuixi. The defending commander abandoned the pass and fled; Li Dingguo suffered successive defeats at Anlong, and Zhu Youlang fled to Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 明年正月三日，大兵入雲南，由榔走騰越。

translations.literal: On the third day of the first month of the following year the great army entered Yunnan; Youlang fled to Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the first month of the following year the Great Qing army entered Yunnan, and Zhu Youlang fled to Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 定國敗於潞江，又走南甸。

translations.literal: Dingguo was defeated on the Lu River and fled again to Nandian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dingguo was defeated on the Lu River and fled again to Nandian.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，抵囊木河，是為緬境。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day they reached Nangmu River — this was Burmese territory.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day they reached the Nangmu River — this was Burmese territory.

sentences.zh: 緬勒從官盡棄兵仗，始啟關，至蠻莫。

translations.literal: The Burmese compelled the followers to discard all weapons before opening the pass; they then reached Manmo.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese compelled the followers to discard all their weapons before opening the pass, and they then reached Manmo.

sentences.zh: 二月，緬以四舟來迎，從官自覓舟，隨行者六百四十余人，陸行者自故岷王子而下九百余人，期會於緬甸。

translations.literal: In the second month the Burmese sent four boats to welcome them; followers found their own boats; more than 640 went by water; those going by land, from the former Prince of Min downward, numbered more than 900; all were to meet in Burma.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Burmese sent four boats to welcome them, while the followers found their own boats. More than 640 went by water; those traveling overland, from the former Prince of Min downward, numbered more than 900. All were to meet in Burma.

sentences.zh: 十八日至井亙。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day they reached Jinggen.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth day they reached Jinggen.

sentences.zh: 黔國公沐天波等謀奉由榔走戶、獵二河，不果。

translations.literal: Prince of Qian State Mu Tianbo and others plotted to escort Youlang through the Hu and Lie rivers, but the plan failed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qian Mu Tianbo and others plotted to escort Zhu Youlang through the Hu and Lie rivers, but the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 五月四日，緬復以舟來迎。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the fifth month the Burmese again sent boats to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the fifth month the Burmese again sent boats to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 明日，發井亙，行三日，至阿瓦。

translations.literal: The next day they set out from Jinggen; after three days they reached Ava.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they set out from Jinggen; after three days' travel they reached Ava.

sentences.zh: 阿瓦者，緬酋所居城也。

translations.literal: Ava was the city where the Burmese chieftain resided.
