translations.idiomatic: Ava was the city where the Burmese chieftain resided.

sentences.zh: 又五日至赭硁。

translations.literal: After five more days they reached Zhequan.
translations.idiomatic: After five more days they reached Zhequan.

sentences.zh: 陸行者緬人悉掠為奴，多自殺。

translations.literal: Those who had traveled overland were seized by the Burmese and taken as slaves; many killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had traveled overland were seized by the Burmese and taken as slaves; many killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 惟岷王子八十餘人流入暹羅。

translations.literal: Only more than eighty followers of the former Prince of Min escaped into Siam.
translations.idiomatic: Only more than eighty followers of the former Prince of Min escaped into Siam.

sentences.zh: 緬人於赭硁置草屋居由榔，遣兵防之。

translations.literal: The Burmese set up a thatched hut at Zhequan for Youlang to live in and dispatched troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese set up a thatched hut at Zhequan for Zhu Youlang to live in and dispatched troops to guard him.

sentences.zh: 十七年，定國、文選與緬戰，索其主，連敗緬兵，緬終不肯出由榔。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Dingguo and Wenxuan fought the Burmese, demanding their ruler be turned over; they repeatedly defeated Burmese troops, but Burma still would not release Youlang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Yongli reign, Li Dingguo and Bai Wenxuan fought the Burmese, demanding that their ruler be turned over. They repeatedly defeated Burmese troops, but Burma still would not release Zhu Youlang.

sentences.zh: 十八年五月，緬酋弟莽猛白代立，紿從官渡河盟。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year, the Burmese chieftain's younger brother Mang Mengbai seized the throne; he deceived the followers into crossing the river to swear alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighteenth year of the Yongli reign, the Burmese chieftain's younger brother Mang Mengbai seized the throne and deceived the followers into crossing the river to swear alliance.

sentences.zh: 既至，以兵圍之，殺沐天波、馬吉翔、王維恭、魏豹等四十有二人，詳《任國璽傳》。

translations.literal: Once they arrived, his troops surrounded them and killed Mu Tianbo, Ma Jixiang, Wang Weigong, Wei Bao, and forty-two others in all — detailed in the "Biography of Ren Guoxi."
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrived, his troops surrounded them and killed Mu Tianbo, Ma Jixiang, Wang Weigong, Wei Bao, and forty-two others in all; for details see the "Biography of Ren Guoxi."

sentences.zh: 存者由榔與其屬二十五人。

translations.literal: Those who survived were Youlang and twenty-five of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Those who survived were Zhu Youlang and twenty-five of his followers.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大兵臨緬，白文選自木邦降，定國走景線，緬人以由榔父子送軍前。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the great army approached Burma; Bai Wenxuan surrendered from Mubang; Dingguo fled to Jingxian; the Burmese delivered Youlang and his son to the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Great Qing army approached Burma. Bai Wenxuan surrendered from Mubang; Li Dingguo fled to Jingxian; and the Burmese delivered Zhu Youlang and his son to the army.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，死於雲南。

translations.literal: The following April he died in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The following April Zhu Youlang died in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 六月，李定國卒，其子嗣興等降。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Li Dingguo died; his son Suxing and others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Dingguo died, and his son Suxing and others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 永思王常溥，神宗第八子。

translations.literal: Prince Yongsi Chang Pu was the Shenzong Emperor's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongsi (Chang Pu) was the Wanli Emperor's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 生二歲殤。

translations.literal: He died in infancy at age two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy at age two.

sentences.zh: 光宗七子。

translations.literal: The Guangzong Emperor had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Taichang Emperor had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 王太后生熹宗、簡王由學。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wang bore the Xizong Emperor and Prince Jian You Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang bore the Tianqi Emperor and Prince Jian (You Xue).

sentences.zh: 王選侍生齊王由楫。

translations.literal: Lady Wang, selected attendant, bore Prince Qi Zhu Youji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang, selected attendant, bore Prince Qi (Zhu Youji).

sentences.zh: 李選侍生懷王由模。

translations.literal: Lady Li, selected attendant, bore Prince Huai Zhu Youmo.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li, selected attendant, bore Prince Huai (Zhu Youmo).

sentences.zh: 劉太后生莊烈皇帝。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Liu bore the Zhuanglie Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Liu bore the Chongzhen Emperor.

sentences.zh: 定懿妃生湘王由栩。

translations.literal: Consort Dingyi bore Prince Xiang Zhu Youxu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Dingyi bore Prince Xiang (Zhu Youxu).

sentences.zh: 敬妃生惠王由橏。

translations.literal: Consort Jing bore Prince Hui Zhu Yourong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Jing bore Prince Hui (Zhu Yourong).

sentences.zh: 簡懷王由學，光宗第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Huai You Xue was the Guangzong Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Huai (You Xue) was the Taichang Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 生四歲殤。

translations.literal: He died in infancy at age four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in infancy at age four.

sentences.zh: 齊思王由楫，光宗第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Si Zhu Youji was the Guangzong Emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Si (Zhu Youji) was the Taichang Emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 生八歲殤。

translations.literal: He died at age eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age eight.

sentences.zh: 懷惠王由模，光宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Huai Hui Zhu Youmo was the Guangzong Emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai Hui (Zhu Youmo) was the Taichang Emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 生五歲殤。

translations.literal: He died at age five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age five.

sentences.zh: 湘懷王由栩，光宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince Xiang Huai Zhu Youxu was the Guangzong Emperor's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang Huai (Zhu Youxu) was the Taichang Emperor's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 惠昭王由橏，光宗第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Hui Zhao Zhu Yourong was the Guangzong Emperor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui Zhao (Zhu Yourong) was the Taichang Emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 俱早殤。

translations.literal: All died young.
translations.idiomatic: All died young.

sentences.zh: 五王皆追加封謚。

translations.literal: All five princes were posthumously granted titles and posthumous names.
translations.idiomatic: All five princes were posthumously granted titles and posthumous names.

sentences.zh: 熹宗三子。

translations.literal: The Xizong Emperor had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianqi Emperor had three sons.

sentences.zh: 懷沖太子慈然，不詳其所生母。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huai Chong Ci Ran — the identity of his birth mother is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huai Chong (Ci Ran) — the identity of his birth mother is unknown.

sentences.zh: 皇貴妃範氏生悼懷太子慈焴。

translations.literal: Imperial Noble Consort Fan bore Crown Prince Dao Huai Ci Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Noble Consort Fan bore Crown Prince Dao Huai (Ci Yu).

sentences.zh: 容妃任氏生獻懷太子慈炅。

translations.literal: Consort Rong, née Ren, bore Crown Prince Xian Huai Ci Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Rong, née Ren, bore Crown Prince Xian Huai (Ci Jiong).

sentences.zh: 懷沖太子慈然，熹宗第一子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Huai Chong Ci Ran was the Xizong Emperor's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Huai Chong (Ci Ran) was the Tianqi Emperor's first son.

sentences.zh: 悼懷太子慈焴，熹宗第二子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Dao Huai Ci Yu was the Xizong Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Dao Huai (Ci Yu) was the Tianqi Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 獻懷太子慈炅，熹宗第三子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xian Huai Ci Jiong was the Xizong Emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xian Huai (Ci Jiong) was the Tianqi Emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 與懷沖、悼懷皆殤。

translations.literal: Together with Huai Chong and Dao Huai, all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Huai Chong and Dao Huai, all died young.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝七子。

translations.literal: The Zhuanglie Emperor had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 周皇后生太子慈烺、懷隱王慈烜、定王慈炯。

translations.literal: Empress Zhou bore Crown Prince Ci Lang, Prince Huai Yin Ci Xuan, and Prince Ding Ci Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhou bore Crown Prince Ci Lang, Prince Huai Yin (Ci Xuan), and Prince Ding (Ci Jiong).

sentences.zh: 田貴妃生永王慈炤、悼靈王慈煥、悼懷王及皇七子。

translations.literal: Noble Consort Tian bore Prince Yong Ci Zhao, Prince Dao Ling Ci Huan, Prince Dao Huai, and the seventh imperial son.
translations.idiomatic: Noble Consort Tian bore Prince Yong (Ci Zhao), Prince Dao Ling (Ci Huan), Prince Dao Huai, and the seventh imperial son.

sentences.zh: 太子慈烺，莊烈帝第一子。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Ci Lang was the Zhuanglie Emperor's first son.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Ci Lang was the Chongzhen Emperor's first son.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年二月生，三年二月立為皇太子。

translations.literal: He was born in the second month of the second year of Chongzhen; in the second month of the third year he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in the second month of the second year of Chongzhen; in the second month of the third year he was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十年預擇東宮侍班講讀官，命禮部尚書姜逢元，詹事姚明恭，少詹王鐸、屈可伸侍班；

translations.literal: In the tenth year the attendants and lecturers on duty for the Eastern Palace were preselected; Minister of Rites Jiang Fengyuan, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Yao Minggong, and Junior Grand Preceptors Wang Duo and Qu Keshen were ordered to attend on duty;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year attendants and lecturers on duty for the Eastern Palace were chosen in advance; Minister of Rites Jiang Fengyuan, Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent Yao Minggong, and Junior Grand Preceptors Wang Duo and Qu Keshen were ordered to attend on duty;

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎方逢年，諭德項煜，修撰劉理順，編修吳偉業、楊廷麟、林曾誌講讀；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Fang Fengnian, Preceptor Xiang Yu, Compiler Liu Lifu, and Reviser-Editors Wu Weiye, Yang Tinglin, and Lin Zengzhi were appointed to lecture and read;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Fang Fengnian, Preceptor Xiang Yu, Compiler Liu Lifu, and Reviser-Editors Wu Weiye, Yang Tinglin, and Lin Zengzhi were appointed to lecture and read;

sentences.zh: 編修胡守恒、楊士聰校書。

translations.literal: Reviser-Editors Hu Shouheng and Yang Shicong were to collate texts.
translations.idiomatic: Reviser-Editors Hu Shouheng and Yang Shicong were to collate texts.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，太子出閤。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year the crown prince left his quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year the crown prince left his quarters.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月開講，閣臣條上講儀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year lectures began; grand secretaries submitted rules for lectures item by item.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year lectures began, and grand secretaries submitted rules for lectures item by item.

sentences.zh: 七月改慈慶宮為端本宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Ciqing Palace was renamed Duanben Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Ciqing Palace was renamed Duanben Palace.

sentences.zh: 慈慶，懿安皇后所居也。

translations.literal: Ciqing was where Empress Yi'an resided.
translations.idiomatic: Ciqing was where Empress Yi'an resided.

sentences.zh: 時太子年十四，議明歲選婚，故先為置宮，而移懿安後於仁壽殿。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince was fourteen; marriage selection was planned for the following year, so a palace was first set up for him, and Empress Yi'an was moved to Renshou Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the crown prince was fourteen; marriage selection was planned for the following year, so a palace was first prepared for him and Empress Yi'an was moved to Renshou Hall.

sentences.zh: 既而以寇警暫停。

translations.literal: Later it was temporarily suspended because of bandit alarms.
translations.idiomatic: Later it was temporarily suspended because of bandit alarms.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，賊獲太子，偽封宋王。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, the rebels seized the crown prince and falsely enfeoffed him as Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, the rebels seized the crown prince and falsely enfeoffed him as Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 及賊敗西走，太子不知所終。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated and fled west, the crown prince's final fate was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated and fled west, the crown prince's final fate was unknown.

sentences.zh: 由崧時，有自北來稱太子者，驗之，以為駙馬都尉王昺孫王之明者偽為之，系獄中，南京士民嘩然不平。

translations.literal: During Zhu Yousong's reign, someone came from the north claiming to be the crown prince; upon investigation, it was determined to be Wang Zhiming, grandson of Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Wang Bing, impersonating him; he was imprisoned, and the gentry and common people of Nanjing erupted in uproar and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Yousong's reign, someone came from the north claiming to be the crown prince; upon investigation, it was determined to be Wang Zhiming, grandson of Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Wang Bing, impersonating him. He was imprisoned, and the gentry and common people of Nanjing erupted in uproar and indignation.

sentences.zh: 袁繼鹹及劉良佐、黃得功輩皆上疏爭。

translations.literal: Yuan Jixian, Liu Liangzuo, Huang Degong, and others all submitted memorials in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jixian, Liu Liangzuo, Huang Degong, and others all submitted memorials in protest.

sentences.zh: 左良玉起兵亦以救太子為名。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu raised troops also under the pretext of rescuing the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu raised troops also under the pretext of rescuing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 一時真偽莫能知也。

translations.literal: For a time none could tell truth from falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: For a time none could tell truth from falsehood.

sentences.zh: 由崧既奔太平，南京亂兵擁王之明立之。

translations.literal: After Zhu Yousong fled to Taiping, disorderly troops in Nanjing supported Wang Zhiming and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Yousong fled to Taiping, disorderly troops in Nanjing supported Wang Zhiming and installed him.

sentences.zh: 越五日，降於我大清。

translations.literal: Five days later, he surrendered to Our Great Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later, he surrendered to the Great Qing.

sentences.zh: 懷隱王慈烜，莊烈帝第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Huai Yin Ci Xuan was the Zhuanglie Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai Yin (Ci Xuan) was the Chongzhen Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 殤。

translations.literal: Died young.
translations.idiomatic: Died young.

sentences.zh: 定王慈炯，莊烈帝第三子。

translations.literal: Prince Ding Ci Jiong was the Zhuanglie Emperor's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding (Ci Jiong) was the Chongzhen Emperor's third son.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年六月諭禮臣：「朕第三子，年已十齡，敬遵祖制，宜加王號。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Chongzhen the emperor instructed the rites officials: "My third son is already ten years of age; reverently following ancestral institutions, a princely title ought to be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year of Chongzhen the emperor instructed the rites officials: "My third son is already ten years of age; reverently following ancestral institutions, a princely title ought to be granted.

sentences.zh: 但既受冊封，必具冕服，而《會典》開載，年十二或十五始行冠禮。

translations.literal: But once he receives investiture, he must have full ceremonial robes, and the 《Institutional Compendium》 records that the capping ceremony is performed only at twelve or fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: But once he receives investiture, he must have full ceremonial robes, and the 《Institutional Compendium》 records that the capping ceremony is performed only at twelve or fifteen.

sentences.zh: 十齡受封加冠，二禮可並行乎？」

translations.literal: Can enfeoffment and capping at ten be performed together?
translations.idiomatic: Can enfeoffment and capping at ten be performed together?

sentences.zh: 於是禮臣歷考經傳及本朝典故以奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon the rites officials exhaustively examined the classics, commentaries, and precedents of the dynasty and memorialized accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the rites officials exhaustively examined the classics, commentaries, and precedents of the dynasty and memorialized accordingly.

sentences.zh: 定於是歲冊封，越二年行冠禮。

translations.literal: It was decided to invest him that year and hold the capping ceremony two years later.
translations.idiomatic: It was decided to invest him that year and hold the capping ceremony two years later.

sentences.zh: 九月封為定王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 十一月選新進士為檢討，國子助教等官為待詔，充王講讀官，以兩殿中書充侍書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month newly minted jinshi were chosen as revising editors, Guozijian assistant instructors and such officials as draft authors, to serve as the prince's lecturers; secretaries of the Two Halls served as writing attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month newly minted jinshi were chosen as revising editors, Guozijian assistant instructors and such officials as draft authors to serve as the prince's lecturers, and secretaries of the Two Halls served as writing attendants.

sentences.zh: 十七年，京師陷，不知所終。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the capital fell; his final fate is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the capital fell; his final fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 永王慈炤，莊烈帝第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Yong Ci Zhao was the Zhuanglie Emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong (Ci Zhao) was the Chongzhen Emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年三月封永王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Chongzhen he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Chongzhen he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 賊陷京師，不知所終。

translations.literal: When bandits took the capital, his final fate was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits took the capital, his final fate was unknown.

sentences.zh: 悼靈王慈煥，莊烈帝第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Dao Ling Ci Huan was the Zhuanglie Emperor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao Ling (Ci Huan) was the Chongzhen Emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 生五歲而病，帝視之，忽云：「九蓮菩薩言，帝待外戚薄，將盡殤諸子。」

translations.literal: At age five he fell ill; when the emperor visited him, he suddenly said: "The Nine-Lotus Bodhisattva says the emperor treats his maternal kin too meagerly and will cause all his sons to die young."
translations.idiomatic: At age five he fell ill; when the emperor visited him, he suddenly said: "The Nine-Lotus Bodhisattva says the emperor treats his maternal kin too meagerly and will cause all his sons to die young."

sentences.zh: 遂薨。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he died.

sentences.zh: 九蓮菩薩者，神宗母，孝定李太后也。

translations.literal: The Nine-Lotus Bodhisattva was the Shenzong Emperor's mother, Empress Dowager Xiaoding of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine-Lotus Bodhisattva was Empress Dowager Xiaoding (née Li), mother of the Wanli Emperor.

sentences.zh: 太后好佛，宮中像作九蓮座，故云。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was devoted to Buddhism; images in the palace were set on nine-lotus seats, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was devoted to Buddhism; images in the palace were set on nine-lotus seats, hence the name.

sentences.zh: 帝念王靈異，封為孺孝悼靈王玄機慈應真君，命禮臣議孝和皇太后、莊妃、懿妃道號。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of the prince's supernatural sign, enfeoffed him as Ruxiao Dao Ling Wang Xuanji Ciying True Lord, and ordered the rites officials to deliberate on posthumous titles for Empress Dowager Xiaohe, Consort Zhuang, and Consort Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of the prince's supernatural sign, enfeoffed him as Ruxiao Dao Ling Wang Xuanji Ciying True Lord, and ordered the rites officials to deliberate on posthumous titles for Empress Dowager Xiaohe, Consort Zhuang, and Consort Yi.

sentences.zh: 禮科給事中李焻言：「諸後妃，祀奉先殿，不可崇邪教以亂徽稱。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary of the Rites Bureau Li Huang memorialized: "The various empresses and consorts are sacrificed to in Fengxian Hall; heterodox cults must not be exalted to disturb honorable titles."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary of the Rites Bureau Li Huang memorialized: "The various empresses and consorts are sacrificed to in Fengxian Hall; heterodox cults must not be exalted to disturb honorable titles."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 十六年十二月，改封宣顯慈應悼靈王，去「真君」號。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixteenth year he was re-enfeoffed as Prince Xuanxian Ciying Dao Ling, dropping the title "True Lord."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixteenth year he was re-enfeoffed as Prince Xuanxian Ciying Dao Ling, dropping the title "True Lord."

sentences.zh: 悼懷王，莊烈帝第六子，生二歲殤。

translations.literal: Prince Dao Huai was the Zhuanglie Emperor's sixth son; he died at age two.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao Huai was the Chongzhen Emperor's sixth son; he died at age two.

sentences.zh: 第七子，生三歲殤。

translations.literal: The seventh son died at age three.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh son died at age three.

sentences.zh: 名俱無考。

translations.literal: Their personal names are unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Their personal names are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：有明諸藩，分封而不錫土，列爵而不臨民，食祿而不治事。

translations.literal: Commentary: Under the Ming, all the princely fiefs were enfeoffed but granted no territory, given ranks but given no jurisdiction over people, fed from stipends but charged with no affairs of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Under the Ming, the princely houses were enfeoffed but granted no land, given titles but no authority over the people, and fed from stipends but charged with no governance.

sentences.zh: 蓋矯枉鑒覆，所以杜漢、晉末大之禍，意固善矣。

translations.literal: This was essentially a deliberate overcorrection, drawing a lesson from the past—meant to forestall the disasters that befell the Han and Jin at their ends; the intention was sound.
translations.idiomatic: This was essentially a deliberate overcorrection, taking past disasters as a warning to forestall the calamities that befell the Han and Jin in their final days; the intention was sound.

sentences.zh: 然徒擁虛名，坐縻厚祿，賢才不克自見，知勇無所設施。

translations.literal: Yet holding empty titles while consuming lavish stipends, men of talent could not make themselves known, and wit and courage found nowhere to be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Yet holding empty titles while consuming lavish stipends, men of talent could not make themselves known, and wit and courage found nowhere to be applied.

sentences.zh: 防閑過峻，法制日增。

translations.literal: Restraints were excessively strict, and regulations multiplied daily.
translations.idiomatic: Restraints were excessively strict, and regulations multiplied daily.

sentences.zh: 出城省墓，請而後許，二王不得相見。

translations.literal: To leave the city to visit ancestral graves required permission; two princes could not meet one another.
translations.idiomatic: To leave the city to visit ancestral graves required permission; two princes could not meet one another.

sentences.zh: 藩禁嚴密，一至於此。

translations.literal: Princely restrictions were so severe as to reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: Princely restrictions had grown so severe as to reach this point.

sentences.zh: 當太祖時，宗藩備邊，軍戎受制，贊儀疏屬，且令遍歷各國，使通親親。

translations.literal: In the time of the Founding Emperor, imperial clansmen garrisoned the frontier and military command answered to them; ceremonial aides and distant kinsmen were dispatched, and moreover they were ordered to travel through the various states so as to cultivate kinship ties.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of the Founding Emperor, imperial clansmen garrisoned the frontier and held military command; ceremonial aides and distant kinsmen were sent out, and they were moreover ordered to travel through the various states to maintain bonds of kinship.

sentences.zh: 然則法網之繁，起自中葉，豈太祖眾建屏藩初計哉！

translations.literal: Thus the dense legal net arose from the dynasty's middle period—it was hardly what the Founding Emperor intended when he broadly planted princely screens around the realm!
translations.idiomatic: Thus the dense legal net arose from the dynasty's middle period—hardly what the Founding Emperor intended when he broadly planted princely screens around the realm!
